human_tolerance.notes: Judgement: breeding habitat is described as open pine woods; no source here establishes garden or urban use.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Authored estimate (low confidence). The sources checked give no breeding months; the Wikipedia article says only that breeding habitat is open pine woods in eastern North America.

vocalizations.description: Musical trill (Wikipedia, Behavior section). The sources checked give no seasonal or time-of-day detail beyond this description.
Slurred chip calls (Wikipedia, Behavior section). Using this call as the alarm is an authored mapping, not a sourced alarm-call description.

taxonomy.note: GBIF usage 7341816 is ACCEPTED, SPECIES rank, matched EXACT. ITIS TSN 950045 is a valid species record. Older names in EltonTraits (Dendroica pinus) and Wikipedia synonyms are not used as identifiers.

external.note: iNaturalist taxon 145244 (active, species rank, Pine Warbler) checked 2026-10-31. NCBI 182907, eBird pinwar and ITIS 950045 via Wikidata (P685, P3444, P815).

conservation.note: IUCN LC from the Wikipedia infobox, which cites BirdLife International (2021).

range.note: US and Canada from 'breeds in southeastern Canada and the northeastern United States' and 'permanent resident in the southeastern United States'. Mexico, Bahamas and Bermuda from 'migrate to northeastern Mexico and islands in Bermuda and the Caribbean' and the subspecies list (achrustera, Bahamas). Other Caribbean islands were not named in the sources and are omitted.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat columns: ground 20, midhigh 80 (other strata 0). Mapped to ground 0.2 and arboreal 0.8 (midhigh placed under arboreal).

habitat.resources.note: Weights from EltonTraits diet percentages (invertebrate 70, fruit 10, nectar 10, seed 10). Wikipedia: insects, seeds and berries; pine-cone and ground foraging. Resource months are not set because no source gives them.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement, not sourced. Wikipedia describes breeding in open pine woods; no source here covers garden or urban use.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Judgement: perch is the shelter tag used for roosting in the shared program. No source gives a roost site.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: permanent resident in the southeastern US, while northern breeders migrate. Scholer row labelled 'migrant' for the US MAPS site. No source checked gives a migrant or winter fraction, so PartialMigration cannot be parameterised honestly (it requires winter_fraction). ActiveYearRound is used as a simplification: the record places the species in the US all year, and the northern migration is not modelled.

seasonal.phases.note: Authored estimate, not sourced. The breeding window 04-01 to 06-30 is judgement. The sources checked give no breeding months.

traits.limb_count.note: Two legs; wings are not counted (schema convention).

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Perching songbird that forages along branches and on the ground by hopping, and flies between perches. The schema has no creep or climb gait for this use, so Hop is the nearest supported gait.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Passerine bird; endothermy is a class-level property of birds.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia Behavior: 'deep, open cups', placed near the end of a branch.

traits.perching.note: Passerine perching bird; Wikipedia describes foraging on branches and trunks.

traits.size_class.note: Tiny, from mass_kg of 11.79 g using the same bins as the Erithacus record.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 11.79 g (source Dunning08). The Scholer dataset also has mass 11.79 for this row, which supports the unit as grams. Wikipedia gives 12 g.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the Wikipedia total body length 5 to 5.75 in (12.7 to 14.6 cm): 13.65 cm = 0.1365 m.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Wikipedia standard measurement 8.75 in, converted: 22.2 cm = 0.222 m. Single value, not a range.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 70, Diet-Fruit 10, Diet-Nect 10, Diet-Seed 10 (sum 100, no vertebrate or carrion). Wikipedia: insects, seeds and berries. The nectar share comes only from EltonTraits.

traits.social.note: Judgement. Wikipedia describes a single foraging bird in a mixed-species flock only as a vagrant record. Pair and group_size [1,2] are authored.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: a songbird that forages and sings in daylight. Not sourced.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: small passerine that flees to cover. Not sourced.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.3, a value between the robin example (0.2) and a more wary forager. No source.

vocalizations.song.note: Wikipedia Behavior: 'The song of this bird is a musical trill.' Season and time windows are not sourced.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Wikipedia Behavior: 'Their calls are slurred chips.' Assigning this call to the alarm role is an authored mapping.

look.note: Authored judgement for the blocky model. Colours follow the Wikipedia description (olive upperparts, yellow throat and breast, white belly, two wing bars), but the values are not measured.

activity.note: Monthly curves are generated by tools/fetch_activity.py (see activity.regions[].sources).

behavior.note: bt-perching-songbird-v1 is the shared perching-songbird program. Its ground foraging by hops, flight to perches, perch-based shelter and spring nest-building fit Wikipedia's description (foraging on branches, trunks and the ground; open cup nests). Default params are kept: nesting months 3 to 6 are not sourced for this species. Judgement, not a sourced value.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Structural stage list (egg, juvenile, adult), authored. No stage durations are given, so none are used.
